facts: The oracle starts the real Streamable HTTP boundary only through McpServiceBootstrap.start(McpHttpServerConfig, IndexPort, ServiceAccountJwtValidator); reflection and an externally prestarted service are outside this proof.
McpHttpServerConfig may bind loopback port 0. RunningMcpServer.endpoint() returns the actual bound MCP URI, and close() must release the socket after every test.

The oracle injects a capturing IndexPort and deterministic ServiceAccountJwtValidator. The server extracts an optional bearer token before validation; JwtValidation.Invalid covers both missing and invalid credentials.

Valid credentials reach normal tool validation. Missing or invalid credentials return unauthorized before tool dispatch or IndexPort.search; the wire proof distinguishes those outcomes with captured calls.
Authenticated initialization exposes only the tools capability, tools/list returns exactly search_logs and get_failure_context, and an unknown tool is rejected before IndexPort.search.

The ten conditions also prove the fixed 15-minute, 200-record, 256-KiB, five-second, and no-pagination limits, plus zero index writes and zero Kubernetes commands. These are observed through the public wire response and capturing dependencies.

This feature owns only the independent MCP HTTP contract oracle. McpQueryService and bootstrap implementation remain feat-006; cluster policy remains feat-010; the Kubernetes journey remains feat-011.
